packageRules.description: Bump the declared range instead of widening it, so lockfile and manifest stay in step
Hold ESLint below v10 while the repos are on v9 flat config. Matches adobe/helix-shared; eslint 10 is a separate migration.
First-party Product Bus libraries and Adobe packages: one grouped PR, automerged, no quarantine
First-party and Adobe majors: grouped, but always reviewed by a human
Third-party packages: batched weekly, automerged, 14-day quarantine against supply-chain attacks
Third-party majors: batched weekly, always reviewed by a human

Split dev dependencies out of the two third-party groups above, so each group is smaller. The renovate/stability-days check is computed per branch, so any single member still inside its minimum release age holds the whole group back; smaller groups reach a fully-aged state more often. Split by depType rather than by package name so it needs no maintenance as dependencies change. These rules come after the catch-all rules above and therefore override only their groupName, inheriting automerge, schedule and minimumReleaseAge.
Same dev/runtime split as above, for major updates.

Keep the ESLint toolchain moving as one unit. eslint and @adobe/eslint-config-helix are peer-linked but land in different groups by scope, so without this they can never be bumped in the same PR and each update fails to install on its own. Comes after the group rules above so it overrides their groupName.
ESLint toolchain majors: one PR, always reviewed by a human.

Renovate cannot enforce a minimum release age on these update types, because they carry no usable release timestamp. Leaving them subject to minimumReleaseAge makes the branch-level renovate/stability-days check go permanently yellow, which silently blocks automerge forever. Mirrors the carve-outs in Renovate's own security:minimumReleaseAge presets.

Digest updates do have a release timestamp at lookup time, but the branch stage does not always carry it forward (renovatebot/renovate#45236), which strands the stability check in a permanently pending state. Accept a timestamp when one is available instead of requiring it.
